items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: And I remember even this McGilvery guy, Art, helped me down to the station with my clothes.

ctx.x: And the superintendent's son, Art McGilvery was his name, I remember. He said something to me or pushed me or something like that and I got mad and I started hitting him and knocked him through a glass door and he got out. And they really, there was the typical scene. It was snowing outside and they just made a big bag out of my clothes, clothing and wrapped it up in a bag, a paper bag and gave me three cents car fare to go to where my father was living in Oak Park. He had a room there someplace.
And I remember even this McGilvery guy, Art, helped me down to the station with my clothes.
